legend: Crowded tissue fragment consisting of cells with moderate to high N:C ratios, with nuclei showing mild variation in nuclear size and shape and eccentric cytoplasm. No myoepithelial cells on the tissue fragments or bare bipolar nuclei in the background are seen. (Giemsa)

legend: Columnar cells seen singly and in minute tissue fragments, some of which show parallel nuclear arrays. The cells show mildly pleomorphic oval nuclei, fine granular nuclear chromatin, and indistinct nucleoli. (Giemsa)

diagnosis: Papillary low- to intermediate-grade ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: Columnar cells with eccentric cytoplasm are present singly, in minute tissue fragments which show a parallel array of nuclei, and in a more crowded 3D tissue fragment. Nuclear pleomorphism is mild. No bare bipolar nuclei are seen. (Giemsa)
Solid and cribriform architecture and mild to moderate nuclear atypia, corresponding to previous cytopathology. (Tissue section, H&E)

diagnosis: Papillary low- to intermediate-grade ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: Large tissue fragment with magenta fibrovascular cores (top right) and a loosely cohesive and dissociating sheet of cells with similar nuclei and eccentric columnar cytoplasm. (Giemsa)

diagnosis: Papillary low to intermediate grade ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: Small cohesive tissue fragment of columnar cells showing a parallel nuclear array  and occasional dispersed single similar cells (Giemsa).
Filigree pattern of papillary proliferation, some with fibrovascular cores, some without, lined by columnar cells with mild nuclear pleomorphism. (Tissue section, H&E)

Large papillary fragment with a branching, magenta fibrovascular core that lacks the fibroelastotic features found in intraductal papillomas, and attached crowded multilayered cells with moderate nuclear enlargement and pleomorphism and eccentric cytoplasm. (Giemsa)

Large, cohesive 3D tissue fragment with crowded epithelium and a suggestion of cribriform architecture, and dispersed intact cells and no bare bipolar nuclei in the background. There are small dark but slightly irregular nuclei and apoptotic debris on the epithelial tissue fragment, mimicking myoepithelial nuclei. (Giemsa)
source: Slide provided by the Department of Pathology, Oslo University Hospital. Photo by T.Sauer

legend: Myoepithelial cells are not seen in the papillary filigree of the tumour but are present at the margin of the tumour. (Tissue section, p63 ICC)

diagnosis: Suspicious for malignancy. Apocrine encapsulated papillary carcinoma
legend: Histological section of the encapsulated papillary carcinoma. The fibrovascular cores are lined by atypical apocrine cells showing intermediate nuclear grade atypia (H&E).
Histological section of the encapsulated papillary carcinoma. The fibrovascular cores are lined by atypical apocrine cells showing intermediate nuclear grade atypia (H&E).
Encapsulated papillary carcinoma with characteristic arborising fronds lined by monotonous cells of low nuclear grade (H&E).
An immunostain for p63 demonstrates a lack of myoepithelial cells lining the fibrovascular cores, supporting the diagnosis.

Large tissue fragment showing a branching fibrovascular core covered in crowded epithelial cells with mildly enlarged and pleomorphic nuclei, and no bimodal component of myoepithelial cells or bare bipolar nuclei in the background. (Giemsa)
Fibrotic zone of circumscribed tumour, with branching papillary fibrovascular strands covered in columnar to cuboidal epithelium. (Tissue section, H&E)

Immunostained section demonstrates absence of p63 - positive nuclei lining fibrovascular cores or surrounding the papillary carcinoma in situ. Note the control myoepithelial cells stain the myoepithelial layer of smaller adjacent benign ducts (immunostain p63). (f)
Micropapillary tissue fragments (left) and a large tissue fragment with complex anastomosing fibrovascular cores lined by similar epithelial cells with moderate nuclear atypia. (Pap)

An atypical fragment of ductal cells with moderate nuclear pleomorphism, but no dispersal and overall insufficient features for a definitive diagnosis of malignancy (Giemsa). Histology showed solid papillary carcinoma.

Massively expanded terminal ductules and ducts by a solid proliferation of cells consistent with solid papillary carcinoma in situ, with more irregular proliferations (top left) suggesting invasive solid papillary carcinoma. (Tissue section, H&E)

diagnosis: Papillary low-grade ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: Irregular branching and papillary tissue fragment of crowded cells with fibrovascular core (central right). (Giemsa)

diagnosis: Papillary low-grade ductal carcinoma in situ
